chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ṣafwān, from Ḥammād, from the one who narrated it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning
A man prays wearing a khuff that filth has affected, so he said: “If it is of that in which the salat is not complete by itself, then there is no harm.”

key_terms.الْخُفِّ: a leather sock or foot-covering worn on the foot
key_terms.الْقَذَرُ: filth or impurity affecting the item
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; no legal objection

ai.seo_question: Can one pray wearing a khuff that has been touched by filth?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about impurity on an item such as a khuff worn during salat. It indicates that if the impure item is of a type that does not by itself constitute sufficient covering for salat, then praying with it does not present a problem.
